Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Lisa Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Lisa Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Reynolds, Chief Operating Officer; Mike Harlan, VP of Exploration; and John Ramirez, VP of Marketing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Lisa, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices around $72 WTI. We achieved robust adjusted EBITDA of $4.2 billion, up 15% year-over-year, alongside impressive free cash flow generation. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on capital allocation priorities, balancing dividends, buybacks, and high-return reinvestments. We are focused on maintaining production guidance amid key basin dynamics. Further, we are working on optimizing debt levels and leverage ratios for maximum flexibility. We continue to advance future development plans with substantial resource potential across our portfolio. Finally, we are taking steps to enhance refining segment performance through higher throughput and efficiency gains.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $18.5 billion, up 18% year-over-year. Operating income was $3.1 billion, and net income was $2.2 billion. We generated $2.8 billion in free cash flow and returned $1.1 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $5.2 billion in total debt and $1.15 billion in cash.

Let me expand on that balance sheet strength, particularly our debt levels, net debt position, and leverage ratios, which highlight the resilience and flexibility of our capital structure even in a volatile macro backdrop. With Brent averaging $82 per barrel in the quarter and WTI at $78, our upstream assets in the Permian and Bakken produced over $850 million in free cash flow in Q3 alone, enabling meaningful deleveraging alongside our high-return development efforts.

Starting with the numbers: As of September 30th, total gross debt is $5.2 billion, including $500 million drawn on our revolving credit facility, $1.8 billion in term loans from our 2022 syndicated facility, and $2.9 billion in fixed-rate senior unsecured notes—mainly the 4.75% notes due 2029 and 5.375% notes due 2032, issued last year at favorable spreads. This reflects a slight sequential uptick from Q2 due to a tactical revolver draw for Permian completions ahead of gas demand peaks. We closed with $1.15 billion in cash, supported by $400 million in working capital gains from optimized payables, receivables, and hedging on 65% of oil output at a $72 blended floor.

Net debt stands at $4.05 billion, down 12% year-over-year from Q2 2023's $4.6 billion and 22% from the post-acquisition peak. This excludes $750 million undrawn on our $3.5 billion revolver, ensuring strong liquidity. Trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA is $2.75 billion, up 15% organically from 8% production growth to 325,000 BOE/d and 10% higher realized prices.

Leverage metrics are at their best in five years: net debt-to-EBITDA at 1.5x, below our 1.0-1.5x target and improved 25% from 2.0x at 2023 year-end—outpacing peers like Occidental at 1.8x. Gross debt-to-EBITDA is 1.9x, debt-to-capitalization 28%, providing firepower for M&A like our recent Delaware Basin bolt-ons. Covenants are solid with 4.5x headroom under the 3.25x test.

Regionally, Permian funding uses low-cost bank debt for multi-pad developments with full-cycle costs under $35/BOE via electrification and water JVs. Bakken has delevered via $300 million YTD FCF, pre-paying $450 million in term loans. GoM exposure is minimal at 5% of capex, hedged 80% at $75 equivalent.

Our strategy emphasizes FCF allocation—50% to debt paydown, 30% to dividends and buybacks like this quarter's $150 million repurchases at 8x EV/EBITDA, and 20% to growth capex. We refinanced via a $1 billion tender extending maturities to 2031 at sub-5% rates, with DD&A at $14/BOE and G&A under 3% of revenues. By year-end, net debt should fall below $3.8 billion at sub-1.2x leverage, eyeing BBB rating. This fortress supports 24 months of capex coverage at $60 WTI and positions us as a consolidator.

Turning to capital allocation priorities—dividends, share buybacks, and reinvestment—which form the cornerstone of superior shareholder returns and long-term value in this dynamic oil and gas landscape. Our framework prioritizes sustaining and growing dividends first, opportunistic share repurchases second, and reinvesting in high-return tier-1 organic opportunities third. Anchored by $2.8 billion Q3 FCF—or $10.5 billion annualized— we've generated over $25 billion cumulatively since 2021 through COVID and the 2022 crisis, thanks to our $45 WTI breakeven portfolio.

Dividends are sacrosanct: We declared $0.65 quarterly today, annualizing to $2.60 for a 3.2% yield matching ExxonMobil and Chevron. This shows 12% five-year CAGR at a 42% payout ratio, backed by 18% ROCE and 0.6x leverage. We aim for 10-15% annual hikes cycle-long, drawing institutions like BlackRock and Vanguard, up 8% YTD holdings.

Buybacks maximize EPS: $4.8 billion remains under our $10 billion program after $2.2 billion YTD at $78 average—below $110 NAV per third-party appraisals like Netherland Sewell. We accelerated during $75 Brent softness, retiring 150 million shares for $0.45 EPS boost. At 4.2x EV/EBITDA—a 25% peer discount—we'll deploy 20-30% annual FCF, tapering for M&A like our $1.5 billion Delaware deal.

Reinvestment—50% of FCF—drives growth: 2024 capex $8.2 billion flat, 62% upstream, 25% midstream/Gulf infrastructure, 13% low-carbon. Upstream $5.1 billion Permian targets 850 MBOE/d via 45 pads at sub-$40 breakevens, with hybrid fracs at 450 ft laterals, 3,500 lbs proppant/ft for 25% better EURs via petrophysics and Halliburton diverters. North Sea Judy/Joanne Phase 2 at FID for 40 MBOE/d by 2026; GoM Winterfell Phase 3 tie-backs at $30/BOE opex; Brazil Buzios to 50 MBOE/d. CCUS $1.1 billion including STRATOS 500 ktpa DAC, Permian rig electrification cutting Scope 1 30%, Gray Oak pipeline to 900 Mbbl/d.

At $70+ oil with non-OPEC constraints, Asia LNG, and geopolitics, we deliver 10-12% FCF yield, 8% reserve growth to 4.2 BBOE, compounding hydrocarbons with ESG.

Now, on capital expenditures breakdown for the year to date, mirroring our full-year discipline. We budgeted $2.5 billion for 2023, 48% drilling, 36% completion, 16% facilities to hit 120,000 BOE/d at $78 WTI. Actuals finished at $2.42 billion, 3.2% under, from efficiencies offset by frac intensity.

Drilling: $1.20 billion budget, $1.10 billion actual—8.3% under via RigRight digital tools, Schlumberger DrillOps, Halliburton PDC bits for 1,450 ft/day ROP, releasing two rigs early on 85 spuds. Permian 70% at $650/lateral ft on 12,000-ft laterals; Eagle Ford 20% sub-$700k DV01; GoM 10% flat. 2024 guide $1.15 billion with SuperSpec rigs.

Completion: $900 million budget, $950 million actual—5.6% over for intensity, 2,200 lbs/ft proppant, 45% local sand, Baker Hughes Intelliprop zipper fracs. Permian 65% Slickwater Plus 55 stages, 1,200 BOE IP30; Eagle Ford 25% cluster tests; GoM 10% on budget. Added $120 million NPV10.

Facilities: $400 million budget, $380 million actual—5% under with modular skids, WaterBridge recycling 65%, Permian electrification 30% cutting emissions 15%. Pivot to 55/30/15 in 2024's $2.6 billion for 130,000 BOE/d exit.

This keeps DD&A $11.50/BOE, top-quartile $4.2 million DV01.

I will now turn the call over to Tom Reynolds for an operational update.

Tom Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 325 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought several new Wolfcamp pads online, expected to contribute significantly to production growth.

Regarding production guidance for Q4 2024 and the full year, we guide conservatively for credibility. For Q4, expect total production of 245 to 255 MBOE/d, a 3% to 6% sequential increase from Q3's 238 MBOE/d. Oil at 165 to 170 MBOPD (67%), gas 475 to 495 MMCFD, NGLs 30 to 32 MBBL/d. Full-year 2024 midpoint 1.08 to 1.12 MMBOE/d, 12% growth over 2023's 970 MBOE/d, from core assets offset by downtime.

Permian (~65%): Q4 160-165 MBOE/d, up 5%, from four Delaware Wolfcamp pads with 15,000-ft laterals, proprietary diverters for 20% IP boost to 1,800 BOE/d IP30, Black River recycling saving $0.50/BOE. Full-year 15% growth, three rigs, 120 wells with SLB tech, two weeks Pecos downtime.

Eagle Ford (~20%): 45-48 MBOE/d Q4, up 2%, Pearsall infills 25% EUR uplift via simul-fracs, 55% oil, 8% full-year from $150 million acquisition.

GoM (~10%): 22-25 MBOE/d Q4 despite hurricanes, Lucius tie-back resumption, Salazar first oil Q4 $400 million project 40 MMBOE NPV10 on Chevron FPSO.

International (~5%): 15-17 MBOE/d, Colombia Rubiales CO2 EOR 12% recovery, Egypt three rigs on LNG tailwinds.

Macros: WTI $75-85, Henry Hub $2.75-3.25, 60% oil hedged $78 collars. Base declines 18-20% offset by $2.2 billion capex (65% D&C), LOE $8/BOE via AI, 45% efficiency gain. Supports $1.5 billion FCF, upside Permian inventory 3+ years, risks sub-$70 WTI or weather.

Now I will turn it over to Mike Harlan for an update on our exploration activities.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Tom. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. Our Permian Delaware spans 250,000 net acres offsetting Occidental's CrownRock, with 3,200 gross locations in Second Bone Spring/Wolfcamp, 1.2 MMBOE net EURs from 150 analogs, 1,800 PUDs up 12%, 4,500 unrisked via ML seismic. Eagle Ford 180,000 acres Karnes, 750 2P, 900 MBO IP30, 1.2 BBOE contingent Austin Chalk. GoM Anchor 25% WI first oil 2026 200 MBOE/d peak, 500 MMBOE 2C Walker Ridge. Suriname Block 58 1.5 BBOE prospective, North Sea Rosebank 70 MBOE/d net.

$2.8 billion 2025 capex 65% Permian $35-40 breakevens, 25% cycle time cut via electric frac fleets. CCUS Permian 1 MMtpa 15-20% recovery, 40% rig electrification, digital twins 5-7% recovery uplift. Five-year NPV10 $25 billion at $70 WTI, 85% sub-$45 breakevens, IRR10 >50%.

Recent seismic in Delaware Basin completed successfully, planning 20 exploration wells next year to add significant reserves.

Finally, I'll turn it over to John Ramirez to discuss our marketing strategy.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Mike. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize production value. Our refining segment delivered solidly despite maintenance and feedstock shifts, across six refineries totaling 2.1 MMbpd capacity, Nelson 11.2, Gulf Coast/Midwest/West Coast.

Q3 throughput averaged 93% utilization, 1.95 MMbpd processed, up 2% sequentially, flat YoY—fifth quarter >90%. Gulf Coast 95% at 1.05 MMbpd heavy sours like Maya/WCS at $18 differential; Midwest 92% 415 Mbpd Bakken/Eagle Ford diesel; West Coast 88% 395 Mbpd Korean VLSFO. Q4 89-91% on turnarounds, back to 94% Q1 2025.

Margins $14.20/bbl, down 8% QoQ up 12% YoY, 80% of $17.80 3-2:1 crack. Gasoline 48% yields $22 RBOB, diesel $28 ULSD +15%, jet $5.50. LLS $105 $3 over WTI, sour savings $2.10, RINs $1.80 25/bbl. Gulf $16.40, Midwest $12.90, West $11.50. Hedged 60% $16 floor.

Efficiency: $5.45/bbl cash costs down 4% QoQ 9% YoY. Conversion 98.2%, APC hydrocrackers +2% lights, cokers 85% $50/ton coke. Energy 0.22 MMBtu/bbl -6%, cogeneration. Maintenance $250 million under 8%, Predix 0.8% downtime.

Renewable diesel $400 million adds 20 Mbpd HRD, 1.5B RINs, AI assays 3% uplift. Scope 1+2 35 kgCO2e/bbl. EBITDA $850 million up 5% QoQ ROIC 22%. Strong demand for renewable diesel blends in California market, expanding customer base, significant LCFS credit impact.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Walsh with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Brian Walsh: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on capital allocation priorities?

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, Brian. As I outlined, our priorities remain dividends first with $0.65 quarterly sacrosanct at 42% payout growing 10-15%; buybacks with $4.8 billion remaining opportunistically below NAV; reinvestment 50% FCF into Permian growth, CCUS, midstream. This balances returns and moat at current prices.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning. What are your expectations for production guidance?

Tom Reynolds: Morning, Sarah. Q4 245-255 MBOE/d, FY midpoint 1.10 MMBOE/d 12% growth, Permian 15%, Eagle Ford 8%, GoM 18%, supported by capex efficiencies, hedged, macro tailwinds, risks downtime or prices.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Could you please provide more color on debt levels and leverage?

Sarah Jenkins: Absolutely, David. Net debt $4.05 billion at 1.5x EBITDA, delevering to sub-1.2x year-end, $2.5 billion liquidity for 24 months coverage, primed for M&A and ratings upgrade.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Mike Harlan: Great question, Emily. Our decade-plus Tier 1 inventory—4.2 BBOE 2P, 6.8 BBOE contingent—supports 10-15% CAGR through 2028 at $60-80 WTI, diversifying CONUS to GoM/Suriname/North Sea with CCUS/ESG integration, bolt-ons, JVs for flexibility.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Torres with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Torres: What is the outlook for the refining segment in the coming years?

John Ramirez: Positive, Mark. Q4 dip then 94%+ utilization, margins capturing benchmarks via slate flexibility, renewables ramp for RINs/LCFS, AI optimizations, ROIC >20% funding upstream amid volatility hedges.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
